metaDescription: Six SDS-plus rotary hammers compared on impact energy in joules, motor type, vibration control and cordless or corded power, for real concrete work.
expertTake: The DeWalt DCH293B is the best cordless SDS-plus rotary hammer here, with 3.5 joules, an L-shape body and an electronic clutch. The DongCheng corded hammer is the value pick for a homeowner who needs to drill a lot of concrete cheaply. If you only drill a few anchor holes a year, a hammer drill is cheaper and these tools are overkill.
introParagraphs: An SDS-plus rotary hammer is not a drill with a hammer option. It uses a piston that strikes the bit directly, so the bit chisels into concrete while it turns. That is why one of these tools drills a hole in seconds that would stall a standard hammer drill.
This guide explains what joules and blows per minute actually describe, how safety clutches protect your wrist and where cordless tools match corded ones.

products.name: DeWalt DCH293B 20V MAX XR Brushless 1-1/8 Inch SDS-Plus Rotary Hammer
products.description:
The DCH293B delivers 3.5 joules of impact energy, which puts a cordless tool near the territory of a corded 9 amp hammer. A brushless motor keeps run time long, and the L-shape body keeps the tool short and balanced. An E-Clutch senses a bind-up and stops the tool before it twists your wrist.

Active Vibration Control reduces what you feel at the handles, which matters on a day of anchor drilling. Compared with the DeWalt DCH273B at 2.1 joules it hits much harder. Against the Milwaukee 2912-22 it has more impact energy but is sold bare.

A high capacity 6 Ah or larger battery is the best match. Keep the chuck greased with a dab of SDS grease and wipe the bit shanks before inserting. Pair it with a dust extractor shroud to keep silica dust out of the air.
products.bestFor: Contractors drilling concrete anchors without cords.
pros: 3.5 joules is strong for a cordless tool
cons: Sold bare, so batteries cost extra

products.name: Milwaukee 2912-22 M18 FUEL 1 Inch SDS-Plus Rotary Hammer Kit
products.description:
The Milwaukee 2912-22 is a complete kit with a 1 inch SDS-plus rotary hammer and two high output 6.0 Ah batteries. The M18 FUEL brushless motor and large packs give the run time needed for a day of drilling. It is ready to use out of the box.

The DeWalt DCH293B is stronger on paper at 3.5 joules and larger capacity, but it is a bare tool. The Milwaukee's 1 inch capacity is the standard size for most anchors. The two batteries rotate through a long job without waiting.

If you already own M18 batteries, the bare tool version costs less. Keep the packs out of heat and the chuck clean. The tool bag and case keep the batteries and bits organized on a jobsite.
products.bestFor: Contractors who want a complete cordless kit.

products.name: DeWalt DCH273B 20V MAX SDS-Plus Rotary Hammer
products.description:
The DCH273B delivers 2.1 joules, which is enough for small anchors and rod hanging in concrete. It has three application modes and Active Vibration Control. The lightweight body suits overhead work.

Compared with the DCH293B at 3.5 joules it is slower in concrete, but it weighs less. For installers drilling many small holes overhead it is a better fit. It is also easier on the wrist.

It is sold bare. A mid-size battery keeps weight down. Grease the chuck and store it in its case. It also works as a light chisel for tile with a flat chisel bit.
products.bestFor: Installers drilling small anchor holes overhead.
cons: 2.1 joules is slow in dense concrete

products.name: Makita XRH04Z 18V LXT 7/8 Inch SDS-Plus Rotary Hammer

specList.label: Modes
specList.value: Rotation only, hammer with rotation, hammer only

products.description:
The Makita XRH04Z has a 0 to 1,200 rpm range and 0 to 4,000 blows per minute, with three modes covering rotation, hammer drilling and hammer only. A torque limiting clutch disengages the gears if the bit binds. Its 7/8 inch capacity is the smallest here.

It does not publish impact energy in joules on the listing, so it is hard to compare with DeWalt directly. It is a sensible choice for Makita LXT owners who drill small holes in concrete. For large anchors choose a stronger tool.

It is a bare tool, and LXT batteries are widely available. Keep the chuck clean. Makita LXT batteries are interchangeable with a huge list of other tools.
products.bestFor: Makita LXT owners with moderate masonry needs.
pros: Torque limiting clutch protects the gears

products.name: DongCheng 1-1/8 Inch SDS-Plus Rotary Hammer with 9.2 Amp Motor
products.description:
The DongCheng corded hammer states 3.6 joules from a 9.2 amp motor at 5,000 blows per minute, slightly more than the DeWalt DCH293B. It has a mechanical safety clutch and two modes, rotary hammer and chisel only. The kit includes bits and chisels.

A corded tool provides constant power and costs far less than a cordless one. It is heavier than the cordless models and tethered to an outlet. Compared with the ENEACRO it has a lower amp rating but a more compact size.

Brand support is thinner than DeWalt or Milwaukee, so check the warranty. Use a heavy extension cord and keep vents clear. Include spare bits in your first purchase, since the supplied ones are for starters.
products.bestFor: Homeowners who need to drill much concrete cheaply.
pros: Mechanical safety clutch protects the wrist

products.name: ENEACRO 1-1/4 Inch SDS-Plus 13 Amp Rotary Hammer
products.description:
The ENEACRO has a 13 amp motor and 5.5 ft-lbs of impact energy, with four functions including drill only and chisel modes. A safety clutch protects against jams, and vibration control reduces fatigue. Its 1-1/4 inch capacity is the largest in this lineup.

Compared with the DongCheng's 9.2 amps it is stronger, and compared with the cordless DeWalt DCH293B it is far cheaper. It is also heavier, so it is a tool for floors and walls rather than ceilings. It suits larger holes and light demolition.

Warranty and parts depend on the seller. Use a heavy gauge extension cord and keep vents clean. The tool is heavy enough that a good stance matters as much as the clutch.
products.bestFor: Heavy concrete work on a budget.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Joules measure the energy of each hammer blow, and it is the best spec for comparing rotary hammers. The DeWalt DCH293B states 3.5 joules and the DCH273B 2.1 joules. The DongCheng quotes 3.6 joules. A figure above 3 joules suits 1/2 inch to 1 inch anchors in concrete. Do not rely on blows per minute alone. A frequent buyer mistake is to compare a cordless tool's joules with a corded tool's amps. Compare joules with joules, and note that the ENEACRO lists only ft-lbs, so treat its figure as a different yardstick.

Corded hammers such as the DongCheng and ENEACRO deliver constant power at low cost. Cordless tools like the Milwaukee 2912-22 free you from cords. A high capacity 6 Ah battery is needed for a day of drilling. Pick corded if you drill near outlets. Battery capacity decides how many holes you drill per charge, and a 6 Ah pack typically beats a 2 Ah pack by a wide margin. Corded tools also avoid the battery cost, which can match the price of the tool.

A binding bit can twist the tool violently. The DeWalt DCH293B has an E-Clutch, and the Makita XRH04Z a torque limiting clutch. Mechanical clutches on the corded tools also protect the wrist. Never buy a hammer without a clutch. Always use the side handle and keep your body braced, since a clutch reduces injury but cannot remove the kick of a jammed bit. Hitting rebar is the classic cause of a jam.

Long sessions on concrete tire the hands. Active Vibration Control on the DeWalt tools reduces it. Cheaper tools use basic dampening. Check handles for a side handle too. Vibration injuries build up over years, so low vibration is a long term health factor. If you drill concrete for hours at a stretch, favor tools with dampened handles.

A heavy corded hammer is fine on a floor, but overhead it wears you down. The DeWalt DCH273B is lighter than the DCH293B, and the L-shape suits ceiling work. Choose weight for how you work. Overhead anchors in a ceiling are where weight hurts most, which is why the DCH273B suits installers. If your work is on floors, weight is less of a concern.

SDS-plus bits come in 5/32 to 1 inch sizes, with 1 inch as common for the class. The ENEACRO lists 1-1/4 inch capacity, while the Makita XRH04Z is 7/8 inch. Larger holes want SDS-max tools. Check the bit sizes you use. Match bit diameter to the tool: a 1 inch bit on a 7/8 inch rated hammer strains the motor. Use sharp carbide bits and avoid forcing the drill.

specDecoder.meaning: The energy of a single hammer blow, measured by the piston strike. A 3.5 joule tool hits harder than a 2.1 joule one. It is the best predictor of concrete speed.
specDecoder.watchFor: Makers sometimes list ft-lbs instead, as ENEACRO does, so convert before comparing.

specDecoder.meaning: The number of blows per minute, such as 4,000 on the Makita XRH04Z or 5,000 on the DongCheng. High bpm gives smoother drilling.
specDecoder.watchFor: Blows per minute without joules is a poor guide to power.

specDecoder.meaning: A bit shank with slots that lets the bit slide in the chuck. It transmits hammer force efficiently. It is not compatible with standard chucks.
specDecoder.watchFor: SDS-plus and SDS-max are not interchangeable.

specDecoder.meaning: An electronic clutch that senses bind-up and stops the motor, as on the DeWalt DCH293B. It protects the wrist.
specDecoder.watchFor: Mechanical clutches also work but may wear.

specDecoder.meaning: A motor without brushes that runs cooler and longer on a battery. All the DeWalt and Milwaukee models use it.
specDecoder.watchFor: Corded tools use brushed motors, which are fine.

howWeEvaluated.title: Impact energy
howWeEvaluated.description: We ranked tools by joules, with the DongCheng at 3.6 and DeWalt DCH293B at 3.5 above the DCH273B at 2.1. Where only ft-lbs were quoted, we noted the difference.

howWeEvaluated.title: Safety and vibration
howWeEvaluated.description: We credited clutches and vibration control, with the DeWalt E-Clutch and Active Vibration Control leading. A hammer without a clutch lost points.

howWeEvaluated.title: Power source and runtime
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared battery kits against corded tools. The Milwaukee 2912-22 includes two 6.0 Ah batteries. Corded models had constant power.

howWeEvaluated.title: Weight and handling
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered L-shape bodies, weight and balance for overhead work. The DCH273B is the lightest.

howWeEvaluated.title: Lineup positioning
howWeEvaluated.description: The DCH293B leads for cordless power, the 2912-22 for kit value and the DCH273B for lightness. The DongCheng and ENEACRO are the corded budget options.

cards.label: Corded
cards.text: Constant power with no battery cost, so more impact for the money. The DongCheng and ENEACRO fit here. They are heavier and tethered.

cards.label: Cordless
cards.text: Mobility with brushless motors and batteries. The DeWalt DCH293B, DCH273B, Milwaukee 2912-22 and Makita XRH04Z fit. They cost more.

howToChoose.note: Choose corded for shop and floor work, and cordless for ladders and jobsites.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: At least 2 joules, a clutch and a side handle. Use carbide SDS-plus bits and clear dust often. A depth stop helps.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The DeWalt DCH293B is best for cordless work. The DongCheng is the best value corded.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You drill concrete weekly or need cordless freedom. The DeWalt DCH293B or Milwaukee 2912-22 repay the cost.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You drill concrete occasionally. The DongCheng corded hammer is enough.

maintenance.why: SDS shanks need lubricant to slide and strike. A dab prevents wear.
Concrete dust is abrasive. It clogs cooling air and wears bearings.
Worn carbide tips slow drilling. Dull bits overheat the tool.
A slipping clutch means the gears are protected. Do not use a tool whose clutch fails.
Corded tools are dragged over concrete. A damaged cord is a hazard.

faq.q: What is the difference between SDS-plus and SDS-max?
faq.a: SDS-plus is a smaller shank for lighter hammers up to about 1-1/8 inches. SDS-max is for heavier tools and larger holes. They do not interchange. Using the wrong shank in the wrong chuck can damage both bit and tool.

faq.q: Is a rotary hammer better than a hammer drill?
faq.a: For concrete, yes by a wide margin. A rotary hammer uses a piston, while a hammer drill uses ridged plates. A hammer drill is fine for a handful of anchors, but a rotary hammer saves hours on bigger jobs.

faq.q: How many joules do I need?
faq.a: Around 2 to 3.5 joules suits most anchor holes. More is faster in dense concrete. Check the manufacturer's recommended anchor diameter before buying.

faq.q: Can I use a rotary hammer as a drill?
faq.a: Yes in drill only mode, with SDS bits. Standard bits need an adapter. Drill only mode is also useful for steel with the right bit.
Yes. Concrete creates silica dust, so use a respirator and dust extraction. A damp cloth over the hole reduces dust when you cannot use extraction.

faq.q: Is cordless as good as corded?
faq.a: Near the top, cordless tools like the DeWalt DCH293B come close. Corded tools still cost less. The gap is mostly in sustained use and price.
